we propose a novel deterministic policy imitation gradient algorithm for continuous control and show that the number of interactions required for training can be reduced significantly.
we propose a novel off-policy IL algorithm which achieves the goal of IL on a variety of complex continuous control tasks with at least tens times less interactions than the state-of-the-art GAIL.
we propose a novel off-policy deterministic policy imitation learning algorithm which can achieve the goal with at least tens time less interactions than Gail on a variety of tasks.

the following question: can we design an IL algorithm which can achieve the goal with less interaction with environment?
how to reduce the number of interactions with the environment in IL algorithms for continuous control.
how to reduce the number of interactions required for imitation learning in continuous control tasks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our DPIG is a novel policy gradient that enables a deterministic policy to be learned from expert’s demonstrations, which is more stable and efficient than the state-of-the-art GAIL.
our DPIG algorithm can significantly improve the applicability of IL to the real-world environment by reducing the number of interactions with the environment during training.

we have developed an off-policy IL algorithm that can be trained with much less interactions than Gail and achieves the same or better performance on a variety of complex continuous control tasks, which makes it more practical and applicable in the real-world environments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new IL algorithm that can reduce the number of environment interactions significantly and achieve the goal of imitation learning.
we have developed a new type of off-policy IL algorithm that is more applicable to the complex real-world environments.

we provide a new direction for model-free, off-policy IL for continuous control.
